title: Add a custom persistent volume as a bind mount directory from the host to the SMLM container | SUSE | Support Center
plain_text:
Add a custom persistent volume as a bind mount directory from the host to the SMLM container
Environment
Help Environment

SUSE Multi-Linux Manager 5.1
SUSE Multi-Linux Manager 5.0
SUSE Linux  Micro 6.1
SUSE Linux  Micro 5.5
SUSE Linux Enterprise Server 15 SP7
SUSE Linux Enterprise Server 15 SP6

Situation
Add a persistent volume (/usr/local/bin) as a bind mount directory from the SLE-Micro host to the SMLM uyuni-server container. 
The reason this could be useful for example is, when you have numerous scripts, wrapped around SMLM bootstrap scripts (used to register new clients) as symbolic links to "/usr/local/bin".
Resolution

There are several ways to bind a directory from the host to the container.

 
IMPORTANT NOTE: Make sure to (temporarily) undo the below steps before attempting a SUSE Multi-Linux Manager version upgrade. The upgrade process is using a script located in '/usr/local/bin' inside the container, if this step is not taken this script can not be located anymore and when attempting to upgrade the following error will be seen:
ERR error="cannot inspect podman values: Error: runc: runc create failed: unable to start container process: error during container init: exec: \"/usr/local/bin/docker-entrypoint.sh\": stat /usr/local/bin/docker-entrypoint.sh: no such file or directory: OCI runtime attempted to invoke a command that was not found"

 

1. The simplest way is to use the host's `/etc/containers/mounts.conf` file.

# echo "/usr/local/bin:/usr/local/bin" >> /etc/containers/mounts.conf
# systemctl daemon-reload
# systemctl restart uyuni-server.service
# mgrctl exec -- ls /usr/local/bin

 

2. As an alternative use a systemd uyuni-server.service drop-in file to set an additional ExecStart argument for the container and add the bind mount flag. Create the drop-in file: local.conf:

# vi /etc/systemd/system/uyuni-server.service.d/local.conf

Copy the entire [Service ] unit from /etc/systemd/system/uyuni-server.service to /etc/systemd/system/uyuni-server.service.d/local.conf.

 

Alternatively copy /etc/systemd/system/uyuni-server.service to /etc/systemd/system/uyuni-server.service.d/local.conf:

cp /etc/systemd/system/uyuni-server.service /etc/systemd/system/uyuni-server.service.d/local.conf

Remove the [Unit] and [Install] units and keep only the [Service] unit in the local.conf file.


Add "ExecStart=" above "ExecStart=/bin/sh -c '/usr/bin/podman run \":

  [Service]
  ExecStart=
  ExecStart=/bin/sh -c '/usr/bin/podman run \
       --conmon-pidfile %t/uyuni-server.pid \


Add "-v /usr/local/bin:/usr/local/bin \" at the bottom of the list of bind mount volumes (-v):

      -v etc-sssd:/etc/sssd \ 
      -v etc-rhn:/etc/rhn \ 
      -v /usr/local/bin:/usr/local/bin \ 
      -e TZ=${TZ} \


Reload/restart the service and test the mounted volume.

# systemctl daemon-reload
# systemctl restart uyuni-server
# mgrctl exec -- ls /usr/local/bin
Cause
Additional Information

For details of the mounts.conf file execute: "cat /etc/containers/mounts.conf":

# This configuration file specifies the default mounts for each container of the
# tools adhering to this file (e.g., CRI-O, Podman, Buildah).  The format of the
# config is /SRC:/DST, one mount per line.
